title: Functions and expressions
description:
Write these functions; use expressions (an `if` or block as the last expression) rather than `return` where you can:

```rust
fn is_leap_year(year: i32) -> bool
fn clock(minutes: i32) -> String          // minutes after midnight as "h:mm": 125 is "2:05"; wraps around, -30 is "23:30"
fn digit_sum(n: i64) -> u32               // ignoring the sign
fn gcd(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64             // Euclid; gcd(0, 0) is 0
fn sign_word(x: f64) -> &'static str      // "negative", "zero" or "positive"
```
hints: Loops come in lesson 1.04; here a function can call itself instead (**recursion**), as long as some case stops: `fn factorial(n: u64) -> u64 { if n == 0 { 1 } else { n * factorial(n - 1) } }`. `gcd(a, b)` is `gcd(b, a % b)` until `b` is 0, and the digit sum of `n` is `n % 10` plus the digit sum of `n / 10` (a helper function taking a `u64` is fine).
`minutes.rem_euclid(1440)` is always between 0 and 1439, unlike `%`, which keeps the sign of `minutes`. `{:02}` pads to two digits.
`i64::MIN` cannot be negated as an `i64`; `n.unsigned_abs()` gives its size as a `u64`.
